note: Restores the frontmost depth plane to the two vector styles whose plate specs silently dropped it, so the plated composite is the picture the generator drew.
retune_reasons: Found 2026-08-13 while cutting reserves into the vector lane. `radiant-orb` and `halftone-horizon` each draw FOUR depth planes and their styles named THREE, so the frontmost plane of each was never composited into a plate and never reached the delivered image. `pale-moon` shipped without its ground and `tidal-halftone` shipped without its sea - which is the subject of the picture.

The tell was a legibility measurement: tidal-halftone's reserved region read as uniform blank paper at 0.911 across the whole rectangle. A halftone of an ocean is not uniform anything. The region was blank because the sea was not there.

This is not a limit of the plate model. `maxPlates` is 3 and all four generators draw within it - `colonnade` also draws four planes and MERGES two of them into one plate (`planes: [distance, headland]`), which is exactly the accommodation the model provides. These two styles omitted rather than merged, and nothing refused them.

pale-moon: the `orb` plate now carries [orb, ground]. The ground is the surface the orb sits above and belongs in front of the orb's own glow, so it joins the frontmost plate rather than starting a fourth.

tidal-halftone: the `headland` plate now carries [headland, sea]. The headland is the mass at the horizon that separates sky from water, and the sea is the water in front of it - one plate, front to back, in the order the generator drew them.
Plate COUNT and blend modes are untouched. This restores planes that were already drawn and already paid for; it does not restructure any style's depth model.

`TestEveryDeclaredPlaneReachesAPlate` now refuses this class of defect at authoring time. It was invisible before because the flatten-equivalence proof compares the generator's own planes against the generator's own flat document - both of which are complete - and never asks whether the STYLE's plate spec covers them.
